$comment: 0.x mode: while the major version is 0, the releaseRules below release a MINOR for a breaking change (feat!/fix! or a BREAKING CHANGE footer) instead of a major, so the line can evolve without a 1.0 promise. Once the packages reach 1.0, change that rule's release to "major" and drop this comment. Deleting the rule would not do: releaseRules are tried in order and the first match wins, so a breaking feat would still match the feat rule below and release a minor. CONTRIBUTING.md states the same rule for contributors. The conventionalcommits preset (installed by the shared workflow) is what makes a bare feat!:/fix!: count as breaking; the default angular preset does not parse the marker at all.

plugins.verifyReleaseCmd: out=$(gh release view "v${nextRelease.version}" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" 2>&1); rc=$?; if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then echo "::error::Release v${nextRelease.version} already exists; releases are immutable."; exit 1; fi; case "$out" in *"release not found"*) exit 0;; esac; echo "::error::Could not confirm that Release v${nextRelease.version} is absent (gh release view exited $rc): $out"; exit 1
plugins.prepareCmd: uv run --no-sync python scripts/set_version.py ${nextRelease.version} && uv lock && uv run --no-sync python scripts/verify_release_version.py v${nextRelease.version} && uv run --no-sync python scripts/build_wheels.py && uv run --no-sync python scripts/smoke_install_wheels.py && (cd dist && sha256sum *.whl > SHA256SUMS)
